Applicant proposes to use data from a hydrothermograph, placed in the Bad Creek Project area during July and August of 1973, to calculate the amount of cooling expected from discharging water through aerators proposed for the stream augmentation system. These data would help determine whether the stream augmentation system should be used as proposed, and whether the system would be used to flush sediments from Howard Creek after construction. If discharges are made into Howard Creek, a continuous temperature monitoring system at the point of discharge would be used to ensure that the water discharged would be of sufficient quality to support the trout resources in Howard Creek.
After construction, stream recovery would be left to natural hydrologic processes in order to maintain its natural appearance, although Applicant proposes to assist in constructing instream devices and applying streamside procedures for correcting the possible environmental damage in accordance with reasonable requests from the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department (SCWMRD).
One measure proposed to enhance the spawning runs of trout in the Howard Creek basin is the removal of a log jam at the mouth of Corbin Creek, the lowest tributary to Howard Creek above Lake Jocassee. Presently, migrating trout cannot enter Corbin Creek because of this log jam (Figure 4-5). Applicant suggests that removal of this obstacle could increase the amount of stream available for trout spawning With approval of the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department, Applicant would remove this obstacle. Applicant states that there may be other stream improvement measures that could be made to offset temporary disturbances of Howard Creek (Duke Power Company, 1976d).
Applicant and SCWMRD have recently completed an agreement for measures to mitigate for stream fishery losses that would be caused by the Bad Creek Project. Applicant, through its subsidiary, Crescent Land and Timber Corporation, is providing a 375-acre parcel of land including a portion of Eastatoe Creek to SCWMRD to mitigate for trout habitat lost to the construction of the project. An erosion control plan (Appendix B) would be implemented to protect the streams in the area.
